purpose: Re-audit the full airfield/staging depth around the Marshalls before re-running the first FLINTLOCK-equivalent suppression cycle. Separate resident combat strength, staging capacity, long-range search, water aviation, and same-day tactical contribution.
authority_note: CURRENT authority remains 1944-01-01. This working audit does not create resident units where no dated trace exists and does not add aircraft already counted in the Marshall 136-serviceable baseline.
branch_geography_guards: Midway remains Japanese-held and bypassed; historical US Midway-based PB2Y raids against Wake are not imported.

Tarawa and Makin are US-held after Branch GALVANIC; the settled phrase US secures Gilberts plus the historical operation baseline implies Abemama/Apamama is also US-held as the low-resistance adjunct. This closes an administrative omission without creating a new casualty event.

Historical Operation-RO drain and the historical 4-Dec mass Kwajalein/Roi carrier strike are not imported; local Japanese aircraft/infrastructure therefore remain healthier than historical where Branch losses do not replace them.

japan_nodes.resident_strength: See MARSHALL_AIR_OOB_1944-01-28_WORKING_v003; 136 serviceable center before Jan31 night losses.
japan_nodes.note: Only this layer can provide routine fighter interception over Roi/Taroa on short notice.

japan_nodes.historical_25Jan_anchor: 753 AG 9 land-attack + 752 AG 6 land-attack; no fighter unit listed.
japan_nodes.branch_working: 12 serviceable center on Jan28, decomposed as 11 land-attack + 1 recon/liaison; no free resident fighter/Raiden.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: long-range/night maritime strike, west-side staging and fallback; cannot instantaneously reinforce Roi fighter CAP.

japan_nodes.historical_state: Intact airfield, harbor and seaplane base; no combat air group listed in the 25-Jan Japanese disposition.
japan_nodes.branch_working: 0 resident combat aircraft credited. Facilities are intact and can receive a deliberate Truk transfer, but no retroactive squadron is spawned.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: latent staging/seaplane/repair depth; a pre-staged long-range detachment could operate, but none is credited at 04:30.

japan_nodes.historical_state: Airfield never became operational; limited harbor/seaplane facilities.

japan_nodes.branch_state: Japanese-held; 23-Nov Branch carrier strike heavily suppressed runway/air function; only limited night-staging recovered by early Dec.
japan_nodes.branch_working: No resident combat squadron credited on 2 Feb. 2-4 long-range aircraft may stage transiently if ordered, but this is capacity not inventory.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: southern night/ferry relay and warning node, not a mass fighter base.

japan_nodes.branch_state: Japanese-held; Oct carrier raid caused 60-75% immediate fixed-base function loss, followed by months of repair. Historical Jan-Feb Midway-based PB2Y pressure is absent because Branch Midway is Japanese-held.
japan_nodes.branch_working: Runway/base function materially healthier than historical by Feb; no resident bomber/fighter squadron is invented. A residual local Kyofu water-defense detachment 4-8 serviceable is carried only as Wake local defense, not Marshall OOB.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: attention-tax / staging / local defense; no direct Roi/Taroa CAP contribution.

japan_nodes.historical_25Jan_anchor: 204 AG about 50 fighters; 902 AG about 10 float reconnaissance; 755 AG about 8 land-attack.
japan_nodes.branch_working: Use as regional reserve/repair/staging anchor, not a same-day Marshall fighter pool. No exact additive Branch count is created here.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: fighters cannot contribute directly to Roi/Taroa on 2-Feb morning; land-attack/floats require staging or long-range mission planning.

japan_nodes.historical_25Jan_anchor: Saipan 201 AG ~30 fighters, 802 AG ~5 flying boats, 902 AG ~4 float reconnaissance; Tinian 755 AG 18 land-attack.
japan_nodes.branch_working: Regional long-range reconnaissance/transport/strategic reserve only; not a same-day local fighter contribution to Kwajalein.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: H8K-class long-range search may feed strategic picture; do not add these aircraft to Marshall local serviceable total.

japan_nodes.branch_state: Japanese-held current settlement: 26-34 normally ready, including 4-6 long-range flying-boat/recon, with routine/elevated search clocks.
japan_nodes.same_day_role: strategic warning and route-observability already baked into Central-Pacific mobilization warning; too distant for 2-Feb Marshall tactical fighter defense.
japan_nodes.anti_double_count: Do not add a second Midway warning bonus to the already-realized submarine/DF/search chain.

us_nodes.historical_development: Fighter strip usable 18 Dec and first planes 20 Dec; bomber strip ultimately 7,050 ft.
us_nodes.branch_adjustment: Branch Tarawa organized resistance ends 28 Nov, close to the historical Seabee runway-work start, so by 2 Feb no material field-capacity penalty remains.
us_nodes.roles: B-24/B-25/A-24 staging, Navy fighter base defense, patrol/search/seaplane command and repair.

us_nodes.historical_development: New field accepted aircraft in December; by late Jan part of the 365-aircraft Gilbert network.
us_nodes.branch_adjustment: Capture ends 27 Nov, only days behind historical; the operation itself is also shifted later, effectively cancelling most construction-date penalty by 2 Feb.
us_nodes.roles: southern fighter/attack staging, B-25/B-24 support, PBY/tender operations.

us_nodes.historical_development: O’Hare Field 4,000-ft fighter strip ready 10 Dec, first aircraft 13 Dec, extended to 6,000 ft for bombers by 21 Dec.
us_nodes.branch_adjustment: Administrative omission closed: US-held as GALVANIC adjunct; by 2 Feb fully usable.
us_nodes.roles: fighter/attack and long-range patrol staging; important depth if Tarawa/Makin are congested.

us_nodes.working: rear/outer staging, patrol and logistics depth. Not added to the 365 Gilbert count unless aircraft are explicitly staging through Gilbert bases.
us_nodes.same_day_role: patrol, ferry, replacement and rescue depth; generally not direct Roi/Taroa tactical fighter contribution.

operational_conclusion: The FLINTLOCK-equivalent air fight is not TF58-versus-136 aircraft. US land-based Gilbert air is a parallel suppression/search/ASW system, while Japanese outer nodes are mostly depth/staging/sensor assets rather than instant fighter reinforcements.
Japanese same-day local fighter defense remains overwhelmingly the Marshall resident network. Truk/Ponape/Wake/Nauru cannot be converted into free morning CAP.

US Gilbert land-air mainly suppresses Mili/Jaluit/Wotje, maintains reconnaissance/ASW, and adds selected heavy/medium-bomber pressure to Taroa/Kwajalein; it does not add all 365 aircraft to the TF58 first strike.
